entry_points.text: Timer creation entries accept clock selector, optional notification description and output identifier pointer; present descriptions are copied or converted from user space before delegating, copy failure reports fault.

Timer query, arm, overrun and delete entries resolve identifier through scoped lookup; get fills kernel setting via clock operations then copies to native or 32-bit form; set fetches new spec and delegates.

Clock set, get, resolution and adjust entries map identifier to operations, fail on missing table or handler, otherwise move timespec or frequency structure between user and kernel and invoke handler.

Generic scheduler initialization installs jiffy fallback, refreshes epoch and starts monotonic wrap timer; registration rejects slower sources, requires interrupts held, derives conversion and wrap limits and enables accounting when fast.

Killable and idle sleeps set task state then wait; bounded sleep handles zero and missing expiry specially; millisecond and range sleeps loop until elapsed; broadcast accessors expose mask, wakeup device and reception.

exports.text: Clock identifier selects an operation bundle; monotonic, raw, coarse, boottime and TAI readers map to matching time sources with namespace adjustment where needed, plus low and hrtimer resolutions.

Common helpers implement remaining, forward, arm, cancel, wait, get, set, delete and exit cleanup on a looked-up timer; converters move interval and frequency structures between kernel and native or legacy user forms.
Visible routines are raw and coarse getters, timer signal delivery, timer release and restore-identifier control; accumulation, adjustment, validation, allocation and lookup remain file local.

hazards.text: Rate paths warn once when multiplier deviates beyond allowed maximum, reject wrap with one-time warning, and repair negative fraction by borrowing one second and suppressing next overflow notification.

User copy failures leave state unchanged; paths tolerate busy cancel as handlers may spin on timer lock; fencing prevents use after free and rearm after delete; lock, RCU, copy and warning helpers owned elsewhere.

invariants.text: Advance skips while suspended, bounds elapsed cycles, returns early below one interval in tick mode, consumes multiples without overflow, corrects rate, folds seconds, refreshes coarse cache and publishes shadow.

TAI displacement equals real displacement plus offset; shifted fractions fold to seconds; each new second runs leap handling shifting wall seconds and displacement, decrementing offset and marking set, with one skip after borrow.

Rate path caches tick length and skew, rebuilds base multiplier on change else removes prior dither, adds one step on positive error, and applies delta preserving current remainder while rejecting wrap.

Control validation enforces single-shot pairing, privilege for changes, tick tolerance, normalized subsecond offset and non-overflowing frequency; auxiliary clocks reject leap, TAI offset and pulse controls.

Query reports interval when periodic; disarmed one-shot with delivery reports minimal positive while no-notify reports zero; unarmed periodic forwards expiry past sampled now and accumulates overruns before computing remaining.

Set and sleep validate durations; absolute expiries use absolute mode with namespace translation and never return remainder; lookup requires positive identifier and ownership revalidated under timer lock.

Scheduler reads combine epoch with masked counter delta via multiply-shift sampled under latch with retry; epoch maintenance preserves continuity and rearms wrap timer; wrappers fix monotonic clock and zero slack.

locks.text: Time readers loop on sequence counter until consistent; scheduler publication alternates between two copies so lock-free readers always observe a consistent parameter set.

Timer state uses per-timer spinlock; delivery drops signal lock before taking timer lock then reacquires; creation initializes lock before hashing under bucket lock and links to signal list only while holding both.

Delete and set bump a sequence fence, invalidate owner under signal lock, retry busy cancel and never touch the object after waiting; exit detaches the whole list then deletes each timer with rescheduling.
Delay-test settings and debug-file lifetime use a dedicated mutex; broadcast shutdown and reprogram never wait for the callback while holding the broadcast lock because the callback needs that lock.

state_machines.text: Rearm validates signal and queue sequence and timer validity, else drops; one-shot reports success; periodic forwards by interval, transfers overrun, resets running count, advances sequence and publishes saturated count.

Creation allocates and hashes timer in invalid state then validates and links; failures unwind through unhash and release; delete invalidates, removes from hash and defers reclaim after grace period with delivery extending reference.

Timers move between disarmed and armed; cancel and new-setting install force disarmed, successful arm marks armed, immediate expiry queues signal, delete forces disarmed; overrun counts missed periodic expiries.

Suspend refreshes epoch, stops wrap timer and swaps to frozen reader; resume recaptures live counter, restarts timer and restores live reader; oneshot wakeup clears forced marker then receives broadcast, spurious events harmless.

structs.text: Keeper holds wall and raw seconds, coarse cache, wall-to-mono displacement, TAI offsets, cycle interval with per-interval increments, tick cache with skew and error accumulators, and mono and raw trackers.

Operation bundle groups resolution, set, adjust, two reads, sleep and the timer family; creation resolves clock, validates event, defaults to alarm signal and links timer; retry marker denotes value one.

Scheduler state holds latch, two parameter copies, wrap interval and counter reader; timeout pairs timer node with task; broadcast keeps central device, masks, forced flag and per-processor wakeup pointer.

Encodings cover absolute selection, no-notify delivery, realtime identity, absolute versus relative modes, armed state, busy retry and sleep flavours; failures use fault, invalid and unsupported; tick, offset and frequency ranges enforced.
